newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-N.Elec sees supply j-v equality.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-N.Elec sees supply j-v equality.

text.p: British regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Electric would have a "broadly equal partnership" in its plans for merging supply businesses with another firm, chairman David Morris told Reuters.
He declined to name the Rec involved in talks but said it "may well not be a nearby one."

Northern had raised the joint venture plans as part of a renewed defence against a hostiled 650 pence per share bid from CE Electric, which is 70 percent-owned by CalEnergy of the U.S. Yorkshire Electricity earlier said it had not held talks with Northern on the issue.
Northern said in a statement the plans should result in joint cost savings of over 28 million stg a year.
Morris said talks on a joint venture partner for its Sovereign gas business were "at an advanced stage," and would be "imminent were there not a bid."
He declined to name the company involved in talks but said it was international, with expertise in upstream gas.
Northern bought out Finland's Neste Oy, its previous partner in Sovereign, a year ago under its British North Gas unit.

Morris said the latest defence showed that the company was strong financially, with forecasts of a full year dividend up 17 percent to 50 pence and growth of at least seven percent from 1998 to 2000. Gearing would move up to around 85 percent by March 2000 from previous forecasts of 75 percent.
"We are saying the company is worth at least as much as we said before...and clearly it is worth more than 650 pence per share," Morris said.
CE Electric raised its bid from 630 pence on Friday and drew a deadline on December 20 for acceptances, four days after the UK is expected to decide whether the bid can proceed.
Morris said Northern did not feel that its current defence might trigger an industry pricing review, as did its previous 560 million stg package to fend off Trafalgar House, now part of Kvaerner.
He said levels of return in regulated businesses were broadly in line with the expectations of industry watchdog Offer.
